data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A token bucket that refills request tokens and byte tokens at configurable rates provides a flexible, burst-tolerant budget; exhaustion is recorded as a typed terminal when the bucket is empty and a fetch cannot be satisfied, with the bucket level history for audit.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The simulated clock must be part of the agent's state hash.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent's fetch pattern is bursty, the bucket may frequently exhaust, causing many denied fetches, which could be misinterpreted.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The token bucket adds complexity and may not be necessary if simple limits suffice.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The refill rates must be chosen carefully to avoid starvation or excessive bursts.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The agent maintains two token buckets: one for requests (capacity C_r, refill rate R_r requests per second) and one for bytes (capacity C_b, refill rate R_b bytes per second). Before a fetch, the agent attempts to consume 1 request token and estimated_bytes byte tokens. If either bucket has insufficient tokens, the fetch is denied and exhaustion is recorded with reason 'token_bucket_exhausted', along with the current token counts and the refill schedule. The refill is based on a deterministic simulated clock that advances with each fetch or wall-clock time, ensuring reproducibility. The terminal state includes the full token bucket history.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
